text:
Luke Evangelista came to New Jersey after 253 games in Nashville, and the Devils are getting what they wanted. With him on the ice at five on five they take 61% of the expected goals, five points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among all NHL forwards in wins above replacement last season, which tells you how quietly good he was in a bad Predators year.

The points have lagged: 12 in 21 games. New Jersey has scored 4.3 fewer goals than expected with him on, and his own goals trail his chances (5 on 6.5 expected). He shoots plenty, 56 already. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts his primary shot assists at the 89th percentile among forwards, so the setups are there and the assists should follow. Our numbers say he plays like Patrick Kane and Jesper Bratt. Our range projects 41 to 62 points. On a Devils team that controls play, he's a good bet to look better in March than he does now.
